title: NvMap::PinHandle never frees anything when SMMU space is exhausted (infinite loop, front() on empty list)
explanation: In the `while ((address = smmu.Allocate(aligned_up)) == 0)` loop the code takes unmap_queue.front() without checking that the list is empty (undefined behaviour on an empty std::list, so the else branch with LOG_CRITICAL is effectively unreachable). It then guards UnmapHandle with `handle_description->d_address` (the handle being pinned, still 0 at this point) instead of `freeHandleDesc->d_address`, so no queued handle is ever unmapped and the loop spins while holding unmap_queue_lock once the SMMU range is full. It also locks another handle's mutex while holding the pinned handle's mutex. Trigger: a game that pins more nvmap memory than the SMMU range holds, with handles parked in unmap_queue.
suggested_fix: Check unmap_queue.empty() first and return an error (or break) when nothing can be freed; take freeHandleDesc from front(), test freeHandleDesc->d_address, and remove it from the queue as UnmapHandle expects.
how_to_verify: Shrink the SMMU allocator in a test build (or pin many large handles) and watch whether PinHandle returns; or read UnmapHandle and confirm it is the only thing that frees SMMU space and that it is skipped when the new handle's d_address is 0.

title: IocCtrlEventWait writes events[event_id] out of bounds on the early BadParameter return
explanation: event_id = params.value.raw is guest-controlled and is not checked against MaxNvEvents (64) before the SCOPE_EXIT is armed. The scope exit runs `events[event_id].fails = 0` whenever must_unmark_fail is still true, which includes the `fence_id >= MaxSyncPoints` early return (the slot bounds check comes later, after must_unmark_fail is cleared). A non-allocation wait with a bad fence id and a large value.raw writes a zero u32 outside the events array, without events_mutex held.
suggested_fix: Validate event_id < MaxNvEvents before arming the scope exit (or arm it only after the slot is validated), and take NvEventsLock around the write.
how_to_verify: Call IocCtrlEventWait with is_allocation=false, fence.id=0xFFFFFFFF and value.raw=0x10000000 under ASan; or read the function: the only return before `must_unmark_fail = false` is the BadParameter one.

title: SharedBufferSession::presentation_slot_base is never assigned, so two sessions use the same pool slots
explanation: The pool is sized for SharedBufferMaxSessions = 2 sessions (SharedBufferSlotsPerSession each) and GetPresentationSlot(slot_base, i) offsets by the base, but the field is only read (shared_buffer_manager.cpp lines 332, 419, 422, 434) and stays 0. Two applications (aruids) with live sessions would use the same slot numbers, i.e. the same presentation buffers. Only matters when two processes create shared buffer sessions at once.
suggested_fix: Assign a base per session (index of the free session slot times SharedBufferSlotsPerSession) in CreateSession and release it in DestroySession.
how_to_verify: Grep for assignments to presentation_slot_base (none found); create sessions for two aruids and print the GetPresentationSlot results.

title: SharedBufferManager::CreateSession leaves a half-built session in m_sessions when a later step fails
explanation: The session is emplaced before AllocateHandleForBuffer, CreateStrayLayer and GetLayerProducerHandle, each wrapped in R_TRY. On failure the entry stays: its container session and nvmap fd are not closed, the shared buffer mapping in the process is not undone, and a retry for the same aruid returns ResultPermissionDenied. DestroySession also R_ASSERTs on FreeNvMapHandle, so a half-built entry can abort at teardown.
suggested_fix: Build the session in a local and move it into m_sessions after the last R_TRY, or erase it and release its resources on the failure paths.
how_to_verify: Inject a failure in CreateStrayLayer (for example by exhausting layers) and call CreateSession twice for the same aruid.

title: FreeReleasedRegions drops the record of a GPU-only region it failed to unmap, leaking pages and the byte count
quote: return true; // still mapped: keep its pages
explanation: When UnmapPageGroup fails the lambda returns true, so erase_if removes the ReleasedRegion although the comment says to keep its pages: pages->Close is never called and m_gpu_only_bytes is never decremented, so the backing stays allocated and counted against the cap permanently. Needs an UnmapPageGroup failure, which only happens if the process or its mapping state changed underneath.
suggested_fix: Return false in that branch so the region is retried, or Close the pages and subtract the size regardless.
how_to_verify: Force UnmapPageGroup to fail once and watch m_gpu_only_bytes; read FreeReleasedRegions.

title: IocCtrlEventWait blocks the HLE thread in an unbounded host wait while holding events_mutex
explanation: After more than 2 failed waits on an event, check_failing stalls the application and calls WaitHost, which is `wait_cv.wait(lk, pred)` with no timeout, while NvEventsLock is held. If the GPU never reaches target_value (a fence for work never submitted, a wrong fence, a GPU hang) this thread and every other event call block forever. Whether a guest reaches fails > 2 for such a fence was not confirmed.
suggested_fix: Use a bounded wait, or drop events_mutex before waiting.
how_to_verify: Wait on a fence value the GPU never reaches three times in a row and look for a hung nvhost-ctrl thread.

title: Blocking DequeueBuffer on stray layers can hang the service thread while all layers are invisible
explanation: WaitForDequeueCondition waits with no timeout. SharedBufferManager::AcquireSharedFrameBuffer dequeues from a stray layer that connected with dequeue_buffer_cannot_block=false. HardwareComposer::ComposeLocked returns early when no layer is visible, so queued buffers are neither acquired nor released and a third dequeue waits until Abandon. dequeue_possible is also a single flag shared by waiters woken with notify_all.
suggested_fix: Return an error after a timeout or when the layer is hidden, and base the predicate on slot state rather than one flag.
how_to_verify: Make the stray layer invisible, queue buffers three times and watch the service thread.

title: Container::ComposeOnDisplay holds m_lock across GPU waits and speed limiting
explanation: m_lock is held through ComposeLocked, which calls nvdisp.WaitForComposite (a GPU wait) and, in Composite, SpeedLimiter().DoSpeedLimiting (sleeps up to a frame, longer at low speed limits). Every VI IPC call (OpenLayer, SetLayerVisibility, ...) takes the same lock and stalls behind the composition each frame.
suggested_fix: Drop m_lock around WaitForComposite and the speed-limit sleep, or snapshot the layer list under the lock first.
how_to_verify: Set a 25% speed limit and time vi IPC calls in a game that changes layer visibility.

title: Nx2GpuMemoryRegistry::TrimMappings rebuilds the whole mapping vector on every map/unmap
explanation: Each MapAt/Unmap allocates a new vector and copies every recorded mapping under the registry mutex. 4K tile maps into non-sparse regions are not coalesced, so a streaming game issuing thousands of map jobs pays O(n^2) over a session, on the ioctl thread and with the registry lock that listeners also need.
suggested_fix: Keep the mappings in a std::map keyed by gpu_address and erase/split only the overlapping entries, merging adjacent runs.
how_to_verify: Log mappings.size() and time TrimMappings in a long Switch 2 session.

title: nvhost_as_gpu::Nx2Sparse(create) overwrites an existing range record and leaks its SMMU allocation
explanation: A second create for the same gpu_address replaces nx2_sparse_ranges[gpu_address] with a new SMMU allocation; the earlier device range is never freed or unmapped. The map lambdas also capture the raw gmmu pointer for later GPU-thread execution.
suggested_fix: Free or reuse the existing entry before inserting, or treat a repeated create as a no-op.
how_to_verify: Issue the same sparse create twice and compare SMMU allocator usage.

title: SubRegisterMemory records a wrapped size when last < start
explanation: m_memory[handle] stores `last - start + 1` outside the check that last > start, so a guest-supplied last below start gives a huge unsigned size that later map jobs may use as a bound.
how_to_verify: Send the TIPC register command with last < start and inspect m_memory.

title: ~INx2Vi2Session can spin for billions of increments
explanation: The loop increments the guest syncpoint until it equals m_release_value; if the guest advanced the counter beyond that value the loop runs around the u32 range, each IncrementGuest taking the host1x lock.
suggested_fix: Loop only while the signed distance (m_release_value - value) is positive, as CompleteHandedFences does.
how_to_verify: Increment the release syncpoint from the guest past m_release_value and close the session.
